payload.title: Where is the /goal prompt produced?
payload.body:
Rivals: a hyp command that reads the log, or a skill that writes the prompt from hyp show.
Scenario that separates them: one Goal whose body block has CRLF line ends, given to both writers. The command prints the block byte for byte or refuses it with exit 1; a skill-written prompt can drift from the body and has no exit code to refuse with.

why: Contested question of the grill for issue #113; the owner settled it in the session.

payload.title: hyp prompt is a command that reads the log
payload.body: hyp prompt G --actor A prints the prompt from the Goal's body and the log, writes nothing, and exits 1 when the body has no valid constraints block.

why: Rival 1 of Q-where.

payload.title: A skill writes the prompt from hyp show
payload.body: The owner-grill skill reads hyp show for the Goal and writes the prompt text itself, copying the constraints lines by hand.

why: Rival 2 of Q-where.

payload.title: Settle Q-where by the session's scenarios
payload.body: Rule, fixed before the record: no run is made; the owner settled this in the session of 2026-11-12 and the session is the evidence. Scenarios in the evidence file: (1) a Goal body whose block has CRLF line ends; (2) a Goal body whose block has a bad line; (3) an actor that already has a Result. The command side gives each scenario a fixed output or an exit code. The skill side has no exit code and copies text by hand. H-command is supported when the command side gives a defined result in all three; H-skill is contradicted when the skill side gives none in at least one.

why: Records the owner's session decision as an argued, not tested, answer.

payload.title: Which hyp commit implements hyp prompt?
payload.body: The candidate is a hyp commit on feat/goal-prompt: the prompt command, the warning on hyp add goal, and the skill and doc text the Goal's May change names. A run adds each commit as a Hypothesis whose subject is the base plus that commit's change; a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes it. Each Experiment's verdict rule asks for red on base and green on the candidate.

why: The build Goal's top-level question; its rivals are the commits a run adds.
